decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 10-0.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October suggests that economic activity is expanding at a moderate pace.”

changes.quote: Labor market conditions have improved further, with strong job gains and a lower unemployment rate.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Labor market conditions improved further, with solid job gains and a lower unemployment rate.”

changes.quote: Household spending is rising moderately; recent declines in energy prices have boosted household purchasing power.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending is rising moderately and business fixed investment is advancing, while the recovery in the housing sector remains slow.”

changes.quote: Business fixed investment is advancing, while the recovery in the housing sector remains slow.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Inflation has declined further below the Committee’s longer-run objective, largely reflecting declines in energy prices.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's longer-run objective, partly reflecting declines in energy prices.”

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined substantially in recent months; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined somewhat further; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable…”

tone_quotes.quote: To support continued progress toward maximum employment and price stability, the Committee today reaffirmed its view that the current 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate remains appropriate.
This policy, by keeping the Committee’s holdings of longer-term securities at sizable levels, should help maintain accommodative financial conditions.

This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.82% APR costs about $49.25 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.73% and moved -10 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.66% would fall by about $16.87 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.6%, and employers added an average of 267k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 0.7% over the past year (December 2014); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -4 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.3% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 86%, cut 3%, hike 11%.
